questions.text: Energy Company Financial Health - SSA: Assess long-term viability: (1) Unit economics (CAC vs LTV); (2) Portfolio quality (PAR30, PAR90 - repayment rates); (3) Funding runway; (4) Path to profitability; (5) Currency risk exposure (revenue in local currency, debt in USD); (6) Investor backing; (7) Audit status.
questions.evidence_required: Financial statements, Portfolio quality reports (PAR), Unit economics analysis, Currency hedging strategy
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many PAYG companies struggle with profitability. High PAR (Portfolio at Risk) indicates bad credit/product. Currency devaluation kills business models.

questions.text: Warranty Fund & Liability Management: Ability to honor warranties: (1) Warranty reserve fund; (2) Liability estimation; (3) Insurance coverage; (4) Bankruptcy contingency (who honors warranty if co fails?); (5) Spare parts financing; (6) Claims history; (7) Re-insurance.
questions.evidence_required: Warranty reserve data, Liability analysis, Contingency plans
questions.africa_specific_notes: If company exits, warranties become worthless. Reserve funds essential. Bankruptcy contingency protects users.

questions.text: Business Model Sustainability: Viability of model: (1) Pricing sustainability (covers costs?); (2) Scale requirements; (3) Subsidy dependence (RBF, grants); (4) Market saturation risk; (5) Regulatory dependence; (6) Technology obsolescence risk; (7) Diversification.
questions.evidence_required: Business plan, Sensitivity analysis, Subsidy dependency analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Heavy reliance on grants/RBF (Results Based Financing) is a risk. Pricing must cover high logistics/service costs.

questions.text: Operational Track Record - Off-Grid: Proven experience: (1) Years in operation in SSA; (2) Systems installed / Connections made; (3) Geographic footprint; (4) Retention rates; (5) Repayment track record; (6) Growth consistency; (7) Crisis management history (COVID, supply chain).
questions.evidence_required: Operational dashboard, Impact reports, Historical data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Fly-by-night operators common. Years of operation matters. Scale indicates reliability.

questions.text: Local Presence & Investment: Commitment to the country: (1) Local entity registration; (2) Physical offices/warehouses; (3) Local staff headcount; (4) Asset investment (vehicles, stock); (5) Community relationships; (6) Tax contribution; (7) Long-term strategy.
questions.evidence_required: Registration docs, Asset register, Staffing records, Tax filings
questions.africa_specific_notes: Physical presence builds trust. 'Briefcase companies' avoided. Local assets show commitment.

questions.text: User Impact Outcomes: Verified impact: (1) Energy access tier improvement (Tier 1 to Tier 2 etc.); (2) Economic impact (savings, income generation); (3) Quality of life (study hours, health); (4) Gender impact; (5) Environmental impact (kerosene displacement); (6) Customer satisfaction (NPS); (7) Independent impact studies.
questions.evidence_required: Impact studies (GOGLA standardized), NPS scores, Case studies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Impact claims must be verified. Kerosene displacement is key metric. Productive use impact growing importance.

questions.text: Industry Recognition & Certification: External validation: (1) Lighting Global / VeraSol certification; (2) GOGLA membership; (3) Industry awards; (4) Partner endorsements (mobile operators, banks); (5) Regulatory good standing; (6) ISO certifications; (7) Investor reputation.
questions.evidence_required: Certificates, Membership proof, Awards, Endorsement letters
questions.africa_specific_notes: Lighting Global/VeraSol is the primary quality signal. GOGLA membership indicates adherence to industry code of conduct.

questions.text: Customer References: Verifiable user feedback: (1) Testimonials; (2) Village/Community references; (3) Pilot project results; (4) Complaint resolution examples; (5) Referenceable client list (for B2B/Mini-grids); (6) Social media sentiment; (7) Word of mouth reputation.
questions.evidence_required: Testimonial database, Pilot reports, Social media analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Word of mouth is the strongest marketing channel. Community leaders' opinion is decisive.

questions.text: Consumer Protection & Fair Sales: Ethical sales practices: (1) Sales agent code of conduct; (2) Prevention of overselling; (3) Transparent pricing disclosure; (4) No-pressure sales policies; (5) Vulnerable customer protection; (6) Data ethics; (7) Mystery shopper results.
questions.evidence_required: Code of conduct, Sales training materials, Mystery shopper reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Agents commission-driven, risk of overselling/misleading. Vulnerable users (illiterate, elderly) need protection. GOGLA Consumer Protection Code.

questions.text: E-Waste Management & Circular Economy: Responsible end-of-life management: (1) Take-back schemes (batteries, panels); (2) Recycling partnerships; (3) Refurbishment programs; (4) E-waste policy; (5) Disposal tracking; (6) Battery life extension strategies; (7) Compliance with e-waste regulations.
questions.evidence_required: E-waste policy, Recycling contracts, Take-back records, Refurbishment data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Solar e-waste is a ticking time bomb. Batteries are hazardous. Take-back schemes difficult in rural areas but essential.

questions.text: Gender & Social Inclusion: Inclusive practices: (1) Women in workforce (agents, techs, management); (2) Products designed for women; (3) Reaching marginalized groups (refugees, extreme poor); (4) Gender pay equity; (5) Safe working conditions; (6) Community engagement; (7) Inclusion strategy.
questions.evidence_required: Gender stats, Inclusion strategy, Product design notes
questions.africa_specific_notes: Women are primary energy users (cooking, home). Female agents often more effective. Refugee settlements are large off-grid markets.

questions.text: Carbon Credit Integrity & Verification: Ensure validity of environmental claims: (1) Methodology used (Gold Standard, Verra, CDM?); (2) Verification process (third-party audits?); (3) Double counting prevention (registry tracking?); (4) Additionality proof (would project happen without credits?); (5) Baseline accuracy (kerosene displacement assumptions?); (6) Vintage of credits; (7) Buyer transparency (who buys the credits?).
questions.evidence_required: Carbon credit verification reports, Registry certificates, Methodology documentation
questions.africa_specific_notes: Carbon finance is growing but risks 'greenwashing'. Verification is key.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Energy in SSA: Product quality (VeraSol) and financial sustainability (portfolio quality) are key. E-waste management is the major long-term integrity challenge. Ethical sales practices protect vulnerable consumers.
